item.title: SCP Idea: Dynaroo
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A very large, very angry, very buff kangaroo with a personal grudge against the D-class program becomes a terrifying threat to the Foundation.

Narrative/Hook +
Narrative/Hook -

Central Narrative: The Foundation begins to receive reports of a very large Kangaroo ambushing D-class transports and holding facilities in Australia. Attempts to capture the Kangaroo fail as it only appears to free D-class and kill Foundation staff before disappearing, and it won’t fall for set-ups or traps. After 2 years of failure to contain this anomaly, the Kangaroo is suddenly found in the wild and is easily captured. When the head researcher appears on-site to see the contained SCP, the Kangaroo assassinates the doctor with a powerful kick that splatters him and destroys the containment chamber. After escaping containment, he leaves behind a clue that indicates he’s a powerful guardian deity of convicts and has been hired by a GOI to sabotage the Foundation.

The world of the SCP is filled with attempts to quell powers older and stronger than humanity and the Foundation is well equipped to handle these threats time and time again. Now, they begin to face anomalies newer and weaker in scope, but with enough established history to justify targeting the Foundation for their various crimes. This is just one example of others, tied with events in SCP-5178 “Eat The Sun with Seth Uhar'' and the GOI looking to exploit the SCP’s own containment and research practices from both the inside and out.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The absurdity will make you laugh, but by emphasizing the reality of the physical strength in actual kangaroos will this SCP make you terrified. By slowly escalating the serious tone of the article, the reader realizes along with the Foundation how much they underestimated this anomaly. By the end the reader may feel conflicted about the entity's violence and their true motivations, which reflect the associated GOI's methodology and theme.


Additional Notes: There will be no references to the 2003 film “Kangaroo Jack” in the article whatsoever.

Promise.

Discussed the idea and possible clashes with SCP-2006 on irc.

To pick up back where I had to go, I don't believe focusing on the creature's origins/octopusness is a particularly strong idea unless you have a real cracking idea of a good/powerful narrative from this (why it does what it does etc. in a compelling way). I can't personally think of where I would take this, but as I mentioned in IRC, this has a very similar 'narrative spine' to 2006 right now, not just abilities - even if it's complete coincidence. This needs to be made much more distinct. My only thought is perhaps the foundation, without the constant threat that 2006 poses, does not concede to your octopus and humour it, and how that would affect it/how it would react, but that is just one idea, I would recommend you try and come up with your own way to take it.

I would really advise thinking of other ways you could take this creature, even after cutting it's want to scare things to more a jovial prankster. If you'd like to bounce ideas about this, feel free to shoot me a DM here or on IRC if I'm about.

GL with your writing :)

item.title: Guidance to the oblivious (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Normal

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation's objective is to preserve normalcy, and it stops at that, what about the average people, the people with no connection with the abnormal, caught in the crossfire between different GOIs, SCPs, and end up on the Foundation's casualty report. This SCP aims to somewhat alleviate that. A series of instructions, warnings, one-time-use spells, etc, etc given to the victims of these anomalous incidents (just a portion of them, enough to catch the Foundation's attention) to help them escape the situation unharmed. but the reality is often bleaker than it looks.

Central Narrative: We are presented with the SCP, the set of requirements for its manifestation. Then, we look through the list of incidents it took place in (about 8 ~ 15 I haven't found the goldilocks number to form a pattern or a narrative yet, officially in the record, it would be around a few thousand). The pattern we see here would be that this SCP has pretty much about 35% success rate with success being the receiver will have no other connection with the anomaly and survive(of course) the rest would be either dead (anomalously or not), sunk deeper into the abnormal, recruited by different GOIs (including the Foundation). Then we are presented with some transcript of the SCP's instruction and we would see some changes in tones, sadder, more pessimistic, although more professional, a stand out transcript would show why it did what it did.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The audience would be hooked (hopefully) with the question of "What about the average civilian in the world dwelled within the anomaly?" and the methods that this unknown force behind the SCP utilizes to help the victims and how the Foundation apply them to standard protocols. Then, hopefully, the audience would see how this kind of work affects an individual, people become more jaded but also more proficient at what they do.

Additional Notes: This SCP might be a more primitive + anomalous version of 911 operatives (now I've just realized that…) but instead of you finding their help, they will try to help you. This is my first idea on the site, so a bit nervous, a lot actually. Hope you like it. If not, all criticism is welcomed.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight for SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a normal human male who is nothing out of the ordinary. What makes this SCP anomalous is the fact that everyone somehow finds him incredibly interesting. SCP researchers become obsessed with studying him and are endlessly fascinated with the quite normal test data he provides.

Central Narrative: The narrative would begin with researchers studying basic aspects of the SCP (height, weight, blood pressure, ect.). After getting these numbers (which are all average for an adult male), the researchers become endlessly fascinated with the man and eagerly perform more tests on the SCP. Over time, the tests grow in number as the researchers become more and more fascinated with his average body and mind. Every time a test is completed, the researchers look at the data, cannot believe what they are seeing, and come up with new tests. They continue to hook up machines and the tests grow in danger. Eventually, the man is killed by a test (maybe electrocution? maybe another SCP?). After his death, researchers no longer find the man interesting and fall into a depression as they are no longer able to test on the man.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The article never acknowledges the fact that the data received is ordinary. The writer of the article writes as if the SCP is truly the most interesting man in the world. No one believes the man is ordinary. No one can believe he is ordinary.

Additional Notes: Not sure if this idea has been done before. Any advice helps. Thanks.

No, I think the problem was that all the drama in this piece was related to sexual abuse of a minor. She compelled people to assault her, and since they were being compelled they were technically being assaulted too. While that might be an engaging story, it’s also entirely inappropriate. Worse, the fact that she was a teenager who had to walk around naked made it seem like the sexual assault business wasn’t even there to create narrative tension, but rather to fulfill some disturbing sexual fantasies. The whole thing was just very unpleasant in a whole range of uncomfortable ways.

If you want to see a story about the friction between religion and sin, you might like SCP-4166, which began as a quasi-rewrite of this.

item.title: Seeking greenlights for SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: I plan on adding pictures.

Elevator Pitch:

+ Open
- Close

SCP-XXXX is an event that takes place in the Netherlands on every first Monday of a month, at 12:00 CET. The following phases of SCP-XXXX then take place. These are:

1) A siren, measured about 104 decibel, sounds for 90 seconds. This siren sounds within the borders of the Netherlands from an unknown source.

2) During those 90 seconds, three Heinkel He 111 warplanes appear in the air and fly a route of 10 kilometre. The spawn location and route of these planes are random. A Vickers 7.5 tl antiaircraft cannon with crew will also appear about 7 kilometre in on that route. These planes are like an illusion in the air.

3) About 70 seconds in, the planes come into the cannon its range. The crew fires at the planes and hits one of them. The plane crashes into the cannon, making a dust cloud. You are unable to see the cannon and the crew.

4) At the end of the 90 seconds, the cannon, crew and planes disappear.

Described in one sentence it is basically: ´A monthly illusion where you follow the story of a crew shooting at three planes and you can interact with it´.

Central Narrative:
You follow a crew of five soldiers and a sergeant. During the 70 seconds prior to the shooting, during preparations, they involve in conversations letting you know more about them. They talk about the war and the sergeant in particular about his family, and how he is hoping to see they are alright. Then they get alarmed by the upcoming planes, and the crew dies to the crash.

You can interact with the crew members. There are 2 outcomes:
1. You are a civilian, they say you should go home.
2. Or you fool them by pretending to be a soldier, in that case you become part of the play (you start behaving like a soldier, no communication with you is then possible). You disappear just like the crew afterwards.

The people seeing the SCP don't pay attention to it (think it's normal) because of its effects.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The interesting parts where I want to focus on are the story from the crew and sergeant and what happens when you become part of the play.

Additional Notes:
1. I might have to make the time longer.
2. Yes, the siren is an actual thing in the Netherlands. I figured it could be a potential idea for an SCP.

item.title: Re: Easter Bunny
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Before you read this, I want to let you know that I am not an experienced reviewer. However, this concept is intriguing to me and I'd like it to succeed.

+ Here we go!
- boop

First of all, I feel like the central narrative here is still the elevator pitch. There isn't really a narrative, but more of a description of the SCP.

The eggs are an interesting concept. To me, they feel like SCP-4666's 'gifts', but it's different enough that I wouldn't call the eggs copies of the gifts. However, I don't really understand the

can obtained be seeing the creature the creature, inside are small unknown harmless creatures, entity can speak through cameras and anything left behind in footage will appear when are is not in veiw


thing. What do you mean by 'can speak through cameras'? What about 'anything left behind in footage will appear when are is not in veiw'?

I also don't understand the black eggs. What does it mean to not 'except "him"'? I'm assuming it's the SCP itself. However, I feel like the Foundation would be able to test what happens when the black egg is given, and it wouldn't be unknown. If you want to leave what is in there for the reader to decide, you could redact it.

I like the concept of the grey eggs as a sort of abduction by the SCP, but I think you could be a little more specific about the reflective surfaces and how the person disappears.

All in all, I think it could work, but most of it is too vague and needs some more specific details to help the reader understand the SCP better. For example, maybe change the pre-requisites for the SCP to hide the eggs to be less broad, as there are many people worldwide who do not celebrate Easter. I wish you good luck with your proposal!

item.title: A Plushie Friend
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fiction (as always)

Page Layout (Optional): Basic Article Template, interviews only with tests subjects, normal test logs.

+ Elevator Pitch
- Elevator Pitch

Elevator Pitch: What started out as an idea of an anomalous plushie that would do good things became… well, a Thaumiel-Class anomalous old monkey plushie with a simple backstory that protects (physically and emotionally) the ones hugging it if they are emotionally linked to the object.

+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

Central Narrative: SCP-#### would be discovered by a field agent accidentally, when a little boy hugging the object was run over by a truck and suffered no damage at all. He (the field agent) would keep an eye on the boy for some months, who seemed to have no anomalous properties. The field agent would become a friend of the boy and his plushie. Months later, the boy would give the plushie to the field agent and make him promise to take care of “him”. He said that he would go to a place called “Imagination” and promised he would send letters to the plushie and to the agent every few weeks. The boy later would be found dead at the roadside, but the letters would keep coming. SCP-#### would be brought home by the field agent, who, when, in tears, hugged the object, would hear a voice calming him down. He would later survive a stray bullet with no damage at all while he slept, hugging the plushie. After that, the field agent would bring the object to the foundation site immediately.

+ Hook/Attention-Grabber
- Hook/Attention-Grabber

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This artifact would be kept in a room safe from external groups of interest, only reliable personnel would come into contact with it and SCP-#### would sometimes ask to the ones hugging him to write letters destined to “Imagination”, saying he moved and was being treated well by the Researchers. It would be an object protected by the Foundation against some Groups of Interest, who would want to have SCP-#### so they could become invincible.

+ Additional Notes

item.title: Re: The Dark Lantern
item.content:encoded:
Hello, so here are some of my explanations. Hope this makes everything more clear ;)

Where does the entity come from?

It comes from another dimension that co-exists with our own. It has been in that dimension for an eternity and it occasionally visits our reality to lure more individuals into its pocket dimension.

Why does it need human wood to light its lantern?

The lantern needs oil to stay lit. There is no source for oil in its original dimension. So, when it transforms you, you will become a tree of oil which it will use to keep the lantern lit.

Also, what is the reason that phones and compasses wont work after a person is lost? Are they in a new pocket dimension?

When you hear the song, you will be lured away from the path. Then, when you get closer to it, you will transported into a pocket dimension which resembles a forest in autumn. There, electronic devices will be mostly useless. You can exit the dimension if you don’t lose hope. If you do, you will become a tree in that dimension.
